newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Business chief urges more tax and industry reform.
newsitem.headline: Business chief urges more tax and industry reform.

text.p: The chief executive of one of Australia's largest manufacturing firms said on Thursday that the country's competitiveness depended on tax reform and a co-ordinated industry policy.

"I think Australia's future competitiveness requires us to get on with fundamental reform in the taxation system," said Graham Kraehe, chief executive of packaging, appliance and wine producer Southcorp Holdings Ltd.

"It requires us to make some co-ordinated industry policy and I think until we do those things we are going to struggle to maintain our current competitiveness," Kraehe told the American Chamber of Commerce in Australia luncheon.
The Australian government has recently reopened the issue of tax reform, which includes a possible goods and services tax.
Kraehe also urged the Australian government to do more in business reform.

"I am a little disappointed that while we made some progress in the last year or two on reducing the budget deficit and making changes to the industrial relations framework, there seems to be a view as Australia has done it tough, so we shall slow down the process," Kraehe said.
Australia's competitive ranking slipped to 17th from 12th in the recent World Economic Forum report.
